question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode=none` on non-loopback or private-ingress Gateway binds, and what explicit guardrail is required if it does?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally blocks reachable unauthenticated Gateway startup, while the request would move protection for operator-capable Gateway surfaces from OpenClaw auth to external network controls.

options.title: Keep fail-closed boundary
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and clarify docs that private-ingress no-auth is not currently supported.

options.title: Sponsor guarded private ingress
options.body: Allow reachable no-auth only through a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, documentation, and tests.

options.title: Reject reachable no-auth core mode
options.body: Close the direction as not planned after documenting why OpenClaw core will not support unauthenticated reachable Gateway binds.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and clarify docs that private-ingress no-auth is not currently supported.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a Gateway security-boundary decision, and this handle has the strongest available history on adjacent fail-closed and no-auth exposure hardening.
